newsitem.title: FRANCE: Matra chief opposes Thomson-CSF market float.
newsitem.headline: Matra chief opposes Thomson-CSF market float.

text.p: The chairman of Lagardere's Matra Defense Espace unit said on Wednesday a market float of Thomson-CSF would weaken and possibly break apart the state-owned defence electronics group.
"What some are recommending, floating the stake owned by the state in Thomson-CSF, would not expand but freeze the industrial boundaries of Thomson," Noel Forgeard told Les Echos.

Forgeard added that a float could eventually result in the breakup of CSF. Under a "core shareholders" scenario several groups with different agendas could take a stake in the capital of Thomson-CSF, possibly breaking the group apart, he explained.
Le Monde newspaper reported on Tuesday that Thomson management preferred a market float of Thomson-CSF over a private placement. The company did not comment on the report.

The French government plans to privatise electronics group Thomson SA through the early sale of its 58-percent stake in profit-making Thomson-CSF and a later sale of loss-making Thomson Multimedia (TMM).

The government earlier this month suspended the planned sale of Thomson SA to Lagardere Groupe after an independent Privatisation Commission objected to terms of a planned resale of TMM to Korean firm Daewoo Electronics.

Forgeard also said that provided Matra manages to team up with Thomson-CSF, the new group could seek alliances "on a business by business basis" with other large European groups such as British Aerospace, GEC or Daimler-Benz Aerospace AG (DASA).
In France the group could also consider partnerships with Dassault Electronique Forgeard and CSEE.
Commenting on the likelihood of a cooperaton with rival Alcatel Alsthom, Forgeard said a joint unit could be set up in a sector combining professional electronics and telecommunications.
